Changelog

arraydesign 0.1.1

First release.

Arrays

  • place_receivers() puts receivers on a depth raster on a regular grid, at random water cells or at the coordinates you give. Grid and random methods return exactly n receivers, each at the centre of its cell. Coordinates in latitude and longitude are projected to the raster; a point just on land, within one cell diagonal of water, moves to the nearest water cell with a message. Any other point on land or off the raster is refused with an error that names it, or the first 10 and the count. Points off the raster are refused first; the points on land are named once every point is on the raster. A raster in longitude and latitude or in a projected CRS whose unit is not the metre is refused. The scale of the CRS is measured at the raster centre on its two axes and its diagonals. A raster is refused when any of the four is more than 1 percent from 1, as in Web Mercator away from the equator. The message names the scale and the UTM zone of the centre. A raster whose scale cannot be measured, such as one in a local engineering CRS, is refused as well.
  • coverage_summary() counts, at each threshold, the water cells that at least one receiver hears on its own, optionally for the receivers in the water on a given day (listening). The print of evaluate_array() also gives the cells the array hears, any receiver hearing.

Simulation

  • movement_model() holds step and turn samplers, a time step and an optional switch between moving and resting. crw_model() builds a correlated random walk with gamma steps and wrapped-normal turns.
  • simulate_tracks() walks animals through water only: a step that meets the shore is reflected off it, so no track crosses land. track_control() sets start positions, the start time and a goal that pulls the animals towards it, with the step at which each animal arrived kept in attr(tracks, "arrived").
  • habitat_selection() gives a movement model a preference for a habitat layer, as a coefficient per unit of the layer or as any log-preference function. The walker keeps each step with a probability set by the preference at its end, so the coefficient is known exactly at the scale of one step; tracks record each step’s heading and the candidates drawn per animal. A model without a preference skips the sampler.
  • available_steps() draws control steps from the walk for each step an animal took, for a conditional logit that checks the preference on the true tracks. Its case and stratum columns carry the names of detfield’s used and available points, so one model call fits both: clogit(case ~ depth_m + strata(stratum)).
  • simulate_transmissions() sends transmissions at a random start-to-start delay (tag_delay), at positions interpolated along the track.
  • simulate_detections() gives each receiver one chance to hear each transmission, with the probability of a detfield detection field. It draws an effect per receiver and hour when the range model has one (overdispersion = "station_hour"), and makes trials only while a receiver is deployed when the field carries deployment times.

Scoring

  • evaluate_array() scores a layout in one call: it builds the detection field, simulates animals, transmissions and detections, positions every detected animal-hour with detfield::location_surface(), and scores the positions against the true tracks. Its seed is passed to each of the three simulation steps in turn, so seed = 1 gives the same animals and detections as the arraydesignR app’s run at seed 1. The count of receivers a covered cell needs is control$k.
  • evaluate_array(control = list(likelihood = ...)) positions by binomial (the default) or presence-only grid localization; control$position_model positions with a range model other than the one that simulated the detections.
  • score_surfaces() measures the error of the mode and mean of each location surface, the share of the truth inside its credible region (hit_rate, with a clustered standard error and 95% interval) and the region’s area.
  • perturb_de_model() scales the 50% and 5% distances of a range model, to see what a wrong range model does to the score.

Maps

  • plot() draws tracks, a receiver layout and an array evaluation on the positionR colours: water by depth, land blank, tracks in grey, receivers as yellow rings and a scale bar. The error map of an evaluation colours each scored animal-hour by error class, by default 0 to 200, 200 to 400, 400 to 800 and over 800 m, and draws the receivers that heard none of the animals as white rings. Errors below a first limit above 0 get a class of their own, so every animal-hour is drawn in the class that holds its error.
  • scale_colour_tracks() colours tracks that are the subject of a map, one colour per animal or group, from six colours of the Okabe-Ito palette without its pale yellow: orange, bluish green, reddish purple, blue, vermillion and sky blue, in that order. colours ties a colour to each level by name, such as bluish green for moving and orange for resting.

Interface

  • The functions share argument names: the raster is grid in every function, including place_receivers(); the count of simulated animals is n_animals in simulate_tracks() and evaluate_array(); and the time one step takes is time_step_s, in seconds, in movement_model() and crw_model().
  • Every error that arraydesign raises itself has the classes arraydesign_error_<kind> and arraydesign_error, so it can be caught by class. The exception is an error about grid in plot(), which reaches the caller as a plain error because S4 method dispatch drops the class. The kinds are input, grid, placement, track and field.
  • Coordinates that do not read as numbers are refused with the column, the count and the first such value and its row.

Example data and documentation

  • Example files on Stoney Lake, Ontario, in inst/extdata: the 100 m depth raster, a 48-hour range test and 20 planned stations. Every help example and article runs on them.
  • Get started, vignette("arraydesign"), tests an array on Stoney Lake: place receivers, map coverage, set a movement model, simulate detections and score positions.
  • Three articles: “Design an array for your own water body: compare layouts” (from your own raster, station lists and range model to a station sheet), “Specifying and testing movement models”, which includes a preference for bottom depth checked on the true tracks, and “Simulate and score an array step by step”. Each article is also a plain R script in system.file("scripts", package = "arraydesign").
  • Every page and example measures distance along detfield’s exact shortest path through water, which bends at the shore instead of following the grid. The planned stations are the grid written in latitude and longitude; the round trip through degrees moves each receiver by a few millimetres, so the two give hit rates that differ in the third decimal.
  • The help of movement_model() and crw_model() cites no source for the correlated random walk itself.
